Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
CONTROLS (observed): WASD moves; arrow keys fire in that direction (they do not move); E places a bomb (decrements bomb HUD); wall hint says ITEM=Space — still untested. Death observed: all heart outlines empty and player sprite absent from room; an earlier death showed a bloodied X-eyed body. Approaching a hazard with 2 hearts left can drain to death very fast.

ITEM 'TECH X' (observed): obtained twice — from a red chest in a treasure room, and from a green/white pill floating above a rock in the two-poop room. Grants goggles sprite. Firing spawns a laser ring ahead in the fire direction; it lingers/drifts, grinds overlapping targets, then fades. Ring offset is NOT fixed (observed ~130-200px, earlier up to ~325px), so point-blank shots overshoot and distance-math aiming is unreliable. Sustained fire (~1-1.5s) needed to kill/break targets. Laser is weak vs brown poop but destroys rocks; bombs broke poop piles earlier and cleared rock pockets.

POPO/OBJECTS (observed): In the two-poop room, destroying both poop piles (laser) left a small golden round object with a face-like marking on the right pile spot. The golden object did NOT react to direct contact or to sustained laser hits; coins HUD stayed 00, so its purpose is unresolved (not confirmed to be a pickup). Poop/rocks appear to regenerate on room re-entry. Small yellow specks seen on the floor were never confirmed as collectible coins.

CHESTS (observed): gray metal chests opened by firing into them, or by contact once enemies were dead. One such chest dropped a heart+bomb orb; another dropped a heart. A red heart pickup at full hearts converted into +1 bomb. The torch room's central gray chest embedded in a rock ring did NOT open on contact with no enemies alive, nor by laser hits that landed beside it — likely key-locked or needs another unlock; HUD keys have stayed 00 throughout. Dark chest room: two corner red-lidded chests resisted many laser impacts; unresolved (key/mimic guess). Central red chest ringed by white spikes stayed closed; a corner chest contact earlier cost several hearts at once (mimic/spike guess, unconfirmed). Key-shaped floor sprites turned out to be my own laser particles, not pickups.

BOMBS (observed): E places at feet; blast damages the player — even a 0.5s retreat from adjacent placement cost a heart, so retreat far. A bomb inside a rock pocket cleared rocks but still cost a heart. Bombing the white spike ring removed no spikes. A bomb against cracked/stained right-wall patterns did nothing (likely decorative). A bomb pickup was collected once in the torch room (+1 bomb).

HAZARDS (observed): Black spider enemies in the dark chest room are melee chasers and lethal. White round-faced 'hopper' enemies in the rock-field room are extremely dangerous: they phase/teleport around the room, sometimes ring themselves with spiky gray rocks, and leave large green splatter clouds with scattered green blobs that damage on contact — a green cloud cost a heart, and subsequent contact(s) drained all hearts to death. Corner torches damage on contact (a wall-hugging descent cost a heart). Diagonal rock chains block both straight and diagonal movement; single-axis moves through gaps work far better. Being wedged against rocks produces several no-op inputs; escaping requires a pure single-axis move into open floor, then re-aligning.

TRANSITIONS (observed): Bottom gold trapdoors descend only when standing fully centered. Top gold crown hatches warp from centered below with sustained W. Dark trapezoid doorways are ordinary connections needing sustained walking and fairly precise centering — attempts at the edges repeatedly failed, but the torch room's top alcove DID eventually transition after centering (~x640) and holding W, so it is a real door, not decorative. Right-wall doorways need the correct vertical band (tutorial room roughly y310-400). UNRESOLVED: in the dark chest room, sustained left pushes beside the left-wall door marking failed to return to the tutorial room.

MAP RELATIONSHIPS (observed/guessed): Tutorial room (wall hints, top and bottom trapezoid doors, right-wall doorway). Bottom trapezoid → torch room (central gray chest in a rock cluster, corner torches, brown poop, top trapezoid alcove, bottom gold trapdoor reached and used this run). Torch room's bottom gold trapdoor → two-poop room (central rock, two poop piles, floating Tech X pill, top crown hatch back to torch room). Torch room's top trapezoid alcove → rock-field room (many gray rocks, golden-framed object embedded in the left wall ~x255,y370, white hoppers, top and bottom trapezoid doors never fully explored). Tutorial right doorway → dark chest room (corner red chests, spike-ringed central chest, black spiders). Tutorial top door was earlier thought to lead to the rock-field room. Earlier run's bottom route: red treasure-chest room → gray-chest room with torches/rocks/poop/blue fly → two-poop room. Torch room's bottom gold trapdoor was previously unreached, now reached.

GOLDEN WALL OBJECT (unresolved): in rock-field room; touching it did nothing; laser never landed squarely on it; may be a key-locked door or container.

FAILED STRATEGIES: contact-opening the torch room's central chest before/without a key; firing while too close (ring overshoots); entering hatches/trapdoors from offset; treating laser-particle sprites as key pickups; bombing the spike ring; long laser on inert/mimic chests and on the golden object; lingering near the rock-field hoppers or their green clouds at reduced health; assuming an open-looking lane is clear (repeatedly wedged in the torch room rock pocket — right-side pocket consistently blocked; escaping up/down then pure sideways worked).

ACTIVE GOALS: find health pickups (cleared rooms rarely gave hearts; hearts are scarcest); obtain a key to open the torch room's central gray chest; test Space (ITEM); determine whether the golden object and the red corner chests are openable, need keys, or are inert/mimics; test diagonal gaps of the white spike ring to reach the dark room's central red chest; explore the rock-field room's remaining exits (top and bottom trapez
